sections.content: You know the subjunctive after advice and requests (*te recomiendo que*) from B1 Unit 4 and after *es importante que* from A2 Unit 27. Here you use them for health advice. *Recomendar que*, *aconsejar que* and *ser importante que* introduce the present subjunctive when the person receiving the advice is a separate subject. The subjunctive marks the recommended action rather than presenting it as a fact. You also meet *convenir*, from B1 Unit 4, in two patterns.

items.spanish: Te recomiendo que descanses unos días.
items.english: I recommend that you rest for a few days.

items.spanish: El médico aconseja que bebas más agua.
items.english: The doctor advises that you drink more water.

items.spanish: Es importante que hagas ejercicio con regularidad.
items.english: It is important that you exercise regularly.

items.spanish: Te conviene descansar antes de volver al trabajo.
items.english: It is advisable for you to rest before returning to work.

sections.content: With *que* and a different subject, use the present subjunctive: *Te recomiendo que descanses.* With *te recomiendo* + infinitive, the person is already named by *te*, so the infinitive is just as natural: *Te recomiendo descansar.* *Convenir* works in both patterns: *Te conviene descansar* / *Conviene que descanses*.
